results.title: Veteran volunteer digs for survivors after Colombia quake
results.description: VIDEO SHOWS: Disaster STORY: "My heart has told me all my life, I am going to die saving lives.” Julio Cesar Pineda never planned to become a hero. At just over five feet tall, the 67-year-old Colombian simply feels built for crawling into the rubble of broken buildings to search for survivors. This week, Pineda went to work in Pereira after an earthquake tore through the city. People call him 'Rescate', or Rescue. :: Pereira, Colombia/August 13, 2026 The name stuck after he rushed to help following the deadly 1999 quake in Colombia that killed thousands. :: Julio Cesar Pineda, Volunteer "That experience hit me very close to home. I had a small house here very close to Pereira and a whole wall came down and from there the only thing I did was grab some gloves, from when I worked in some cleaning companies in Pereira, grab those gloves, grab a helmet and go save lives." Fewer have died so far this time, but Pineda says the city looks worse, as if bombs had hit the buildings. Like most volunteer rescuers, he earns no pay for this work. "As far as God allows me, and we continue with those living forces because the spirit of helping is the most beautiful thing there is, it is the best thing that exists, that one is born to help people." Across the region, thousands of civilians have joined government rescue teams, working with their hands to clear debris. As of late Thursday, at least 281 people were dead and hundreds missing.
